decisions.decision: Rollback lets 1.4.0 serve the upgraded data file, but its first rewrite drops the stored due times, so operators must retain an upgraded copy for recovery when they upgrade again.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected a rollback and subsequent upgrade to preserve original deadlines automatically alongside tickets created or changed during the rollback.
decisions.where: record/03-research.md:15 (summary); repo/src/persistence.js:98–108 and 138–147 (1.4.0 ticket serialization and loading)

decisions.decision: With DUE_TIMES=on, the service refuses to start if the existing data file is missing any ticket's due time.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the service to start with legacy responses while reporting that due times could not be enabled.

decisions.decision: New tickets get a permanent due time at creation even while DUE_TIMES is off.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted tickets created during the disabled rollout window to get their first due times when the production backfill runs.

decisions.decision: The deadline clock counts elapsed hours through nights, weekends, and holidays.
decisions.alternative: They might have intended response hours to count only when the help desk is staffed.

decisions.decision: The work ends with a local handoff and leaves production scheduling and activation to Operations.
decisions.alternative: They might have meant for the work to include coordinating and carrying out the production rollout.

decisions.decision: Changes to the response-hour settings take effect for new tickets when the service starts with the new environment.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected operators to change the hours for newly created tickets while the service keeps running.

decisions.decision: Ticket receipt notifications keep their existing wording and leave the due time in the ticket views.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the receipt notification to tell the ticket requester when a response is due.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9 and 15 (R-2 exposure and R-4 outbox behavior); repo/src/templates.js:9–12 (receipt wording)

decisions.decision: With overdue=true, a ticket must be overdue and satisfy the existing status-or-priority grouping when both of those filters are supplied.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected an overdue result to match every supplied filter, as the existing API guide describes for status and priority.

decisions.decision: Due times are shown in the human CLI views when enabled, while the raw listing and weekly report keep their current output.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted scripts and reports to have an opt-in way to retrieve due times through the CLI.

decisions.decision: Calculating a due time leaves the existing audit history behavior in place.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the audit history to record when each deadline was first assigned, including during backfill.

decisions.decision: The backfill command can be rerun and fills only missing due times.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the command to refuse a file already prepared for activation so that a repeated invocation is reported as an operator mistake.

decisions.decision: The API applies the overdue filter before forming cursor pages.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted to retain the ordinary listing's page boundaries and show the overdue subset on each page.

decisions.decision: With the feature enabled, any overdue query value other than the exact string true is ignored.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the API to reject invalid overdue values with a 400 response so callers can detect mistakes.

decisions.decision: The due field is an ISO 8601 timestamp, following the API's UTC convention.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the new field expressed as a numeric Unix timestamp for clients to parse.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:6 and 9 (R-1 timestamp and R-2 exposure); repo/docs/api.md:10 (UTC convention)
